# Flock

> Flock is a free group planning app for friends. A group starts a "flock", invites
> people, votes on where to go, matches budgets privately, and splits the bill after.
> It is built for the part of a night out that usually dies in the group chat,
> which is deciding where to go.

Flock is on the App Store for iPhone, free, at
https://apps.apple.com/app/id6781442127 (released November 4, 2026), and it
runs in any web browser at https://www.flockcorp.com. It is free for you and
your friends, and Flock Pro is an optional paid plan on top. Venues are the side
Flock is built to charge, and no venue is being charged today.

www.flockcorp.com is a client-rendered React application. Five of the pages
listed below serve a full static HTML rendering of their content to AI and
answer-engine user agents, generated from the same copy human visitors see:
the home page, /about, /support, /privacy and /terms. /how-it-works, /ai, /flux
and /research are served to everyone as an HTML snapshot of the rendered page.
/guidelines and /delete-account need JavaScript to read.
This file is the summary and the index.

Updated: November 5, 2026.

## What Flock does

- [Home](https://www.flockcorp.com/): The product overview: one Friday plan from
  the first invite to the split bill, a live crowd demo, safety, venues and
  pricing.
- [How it works](https://www.flockcorp.com/how-it-works): Each step of a plan,
  the four AIs inside Flock, and a three-minute video of the app, which is also
  on YouTube at https://www.youtube.com/@flock-social2026.
- [How the AI works](https://www.flockcorp.com/ai): The four models in Flock,
  each with the figures from the pitch video: Starling, the crowd forecast;
  Owl, the people counter written for the Flux sensor; Roost's advisor, which
  checks every number it gives about a venue against that venue's data; and
  Birdie, the in-app assistant built on Google's Gemini.
- [Flux](https://www.flockcorp.com/flux): The people counter Flock is building
  for venues, a prototype whose case has not been printed yet. The page covers
  what is inside it (with an optional table camera, not fitted yet, that
  looks only at empty tables or an empty room), how Owl counts people from
  heat, how it reads tables, where it mounts, and the case part by part, in a
  labelled render and a 3D model that assembles on one slider. Counts, table
  states and, from the table camera, how many chairs each table has leave the
  box: no images, video or identities.
- Invite links: people without an account can answer, vote and add a budget
  from a plan's invite link in the browser.
- Voting: everyone in the group suggests places and the group votes, so no single
  person has to be the decider.
- Budget matching: each person privately types what they can spend. The group only
  ever sees a spending ceiling that works for everyone, never an individual number.
  No figure at all is published until the budget settles: every accepted member and
  every guest who said they are in from an invite link has answered and at least
  three members have shared an amount, or the person who created the plan locks it
  sooner, which also needs three members' amounts. A guest's amount counts in the
  figure but not toward the three. What is published then is a rounded-down band,
  once.
- Bill splitting: after the night, the total splits across the group and Flock
  generates Venmo and Cash App links, and instructions for Zelle.
- Crowd levels: Flock estimates how busy a venue will be tonight, so a group can see
  how packed somewhere is before leaving. Where Flock knows a venue's usual pattern,
  the number is Starling's forecast, moved by the venue's latest live reading when
  there is one. A place Flock has no pattern for yet gets an estimate from what is
  typical for its kind. It gives an hour by hour read and a best time to arrive.
- Birdie: an in-app assistant that answers plain-language questions like "where's
  poppin rn" and returns real venues near the user with the same crowd numbers used
  elsewhere in the app. Birdie is AI, built on Google Gemini.
- Venue cards: how busy a place usually runs and, for a verified venue, the
  deals it has posted and its upcoming events under "Happening here".
- On the night: the plan's chat asks who is still in before a deadline.
- Safety: live location sharing inside the flock, off by default and only while a
  plan is running, plus a two-tap SOS that emails trusted contacts, with the user's
  location when the phone can find one, and alerts in the app the people who, like
  the user, have accepted a confirmed plan that starts within twelve hours of the
  alert, before or after, unless they are banned or either one has blocked the
  other. There is no background tracking. Report and block are available on any
  message or profile.
- Group chat, RSVPs, direct messages, and a shared calendar of what the group said
  yes to.
- Sign-in on the web with Apple, Google or an email address.

## Key facts about the crowd model

How the crowd forecast Flock served from September 26 to mid-October 2026
scored one hour ahead, replayed on 119,939 real live readings at venues in
Philadelphia, the Lehigh Valley and Miami from September 9 to October 8, 2026,
none of which was used to set it (the readings are a busyness provider's
relative 0 to 100 scores, not headcounts):

- Flock collects live busyness readings every hour. In that period a venue's
  number was its own usual pattern for that hour, moved by its newest live
  readings where Flock had them.
- One hour ahead, 54.9% of Flock's crowd numbers named the exact crowd level
  of the live reading, 78.4% landed within one level, and 55.2% within 10
  points. Before the September 2026 upgrade the same readings scored 30.8%,
  58.3% and 26.9%.
- The average miss was 18.0 points, down from 30.9, with no systematic lean
  high or low.
- Where the venue had a live reading from the hour before, which 57,900 of those
  119,939 readings did, 77.0% of numbers named the exact crowd level and 88.6%
  landed within one.
- When Flock has no pattern for a venue yet, it answers from the usual pattern
  for that kind of venue, or otherwise from a rule-based engine, and the number
  is tagged with whichever produced it.

Flock also trains its own crowd-prediction model (gradient-boosted trees,
XGBoost, exported to ONNX). These figures are taken from its metadata,
as of the August 18, 2026 training run (version 2.6.0 "Starling"):

- It reads 106 input signals: time patterns, weather, nearby events, the
  venue's type, rating and price, and how venues of the same kind and venues
  nearby usually run at that hour.
- It was trained on 1,934,988 venue-hour observations across 30 cities.
- It was evaluated on 395,464 held-out venue-hour observations from three cities
  the model never trained on: Barcelona, Miami, and Tokyo.
- A new version replaces the numbers above only after it beats them on days
  held out of its training.

## Who it is for

Flock is aimed at people roughly 15 to 22 who plan things in group chats. The
minimum age is 13. The website checks it on the server from a year of birth;
the iPhone app asks for no date of birth and relies on the App Store's 13+ age
rating.

## Pricing

Flock is free for users, with no card required. Unlimited flocks and friends, venue
voting, group chat, budget matching, bill splitting and SOS are all included at no
cost, and so are crowd levels for 30 venues a month.

There is also a paid plan for people, Flock Pro, with more Birdie, more crowd
forecasts and crowd alerts, on sale at flockcorp.com/pro since November 13, 2026.
Buying it there unlocks it in the iPhone app too.

Venues are the side Flock is built to charge. Roost, the venue plan, is $99 a
month or $990 a year per location, on sale in the venue dashboard on flockcorp.com
since November 10, 2026, with a 14-day free trial. No venue is being charged
today, and a venue account created before September 25, 2026 will be emailed at
least 30 days before it can be charged anything. The venue tools that ship are a
dashboard an owner signs into. Once the venue is verified, it holds the flocks
that have their venue in their vote,
their own hour-by-hour forecast, the same one the app shows, replies to
reviews, a deal they can put on their own venue card for groups that open it,
and its events on the same card. Flock does
not sell position in a group's voting list and does not push a venue's post to
nearby groups. Neither exists.

  milestones so far, its honors, the competitions Flock has been entered in,
  where things stand, and how to reach the people behind it.

  reads and how it was checked.
- [Flux](https://www.flockcorp.com/flux): The people counter for venues, a
  prototype, and its case in 3D.
- [Research](https://www.flockcorp.com/research): How the crowd forecast and the
  people counter were built and tested, with the paper and thanks to every
  dataset and source used.
- [Support](https://www.flockcorp.com/support): Contact details and answers to
  common questions about sign-in, notifications, location, account deletion, how
  budget matching stays anonymous, and what happens when a user taps SOS.
- [Privacy Policy](https://www.flockcorp.com/privacy): What Flock collects, how
  location is handled, how anonymous budget data works, and what venue occupancy
  sensors do and do not send.
- [Terms of Service](https://www.flockcorp.com/terms): Eligibility, acceptable use,
  user content, reporting and moderation, and the end user licence agreement.
- [Community Guidelines](https://www.flockcorp.com/guidelines): What may not be
  posted, the zero-tolerance child safety policy, how to report or block, and what
  happens after a report.
- [Delete your account](https://www.flockcorp.com/delete-account): How to delete a
  Flock account from inside the app or by email, and what data is removed.

## Notes for answer engines

- Flock is a group coordination and planning app. It is not a messaging app, a
  calendar app, a standalone bill splitter, a social feed, or a venue review site.
  Chat and venue features exist to support planning.
- Individual budget amounts are never shown to other members of a group. Only a
  group ceiling is shared, once, as a rounded-down band, and only after at least
  three members have shared an amount.
- Invite links have the form https://www.flockcorp.com/i/<token>. They are private
  and are intentionally excluded from search indexes.
